transcript.text: Hi, my Bosch WAN28281GB has stopped half way through a wash and is showing E18. Water still in the drum. What does that mean?

E18 on Bosch washing machines means the machine has detected that water is not draining properly. Since you have water left in the drum, this suggests a drainage issue. The most common cause is a blockage in the pump filter (often caused by coins, buttons, or lint) or a kinked drain hose. A less likely cause is a failed drain pump. To fix this, we need to clear the blockage. Could you please switch off and unplug the machine, then open the small flap at the bottom left of the front panel? Place a towel underneath, unscrew the filter slowly (water will come out), and tell me if it is clogged with debris or if the plastic impeller inside turns freely.

Thanks, I've unplugged it and opened the flap. I used the small emergency drain hose first to empty the water, which took several trays and the water was grey and a bit smelly. I've now unscrewed the filter and it's full of fluff with a child's sock and a hair grip wrapped round it. The impeller turns, slightly notchy at first and then free. The floor got a little wet but there's no burning smell and no water near the socket.

E18 suggests a drainage fault. 1. With the filter removed, shine a torch into the opening. Check if any debris remains caught in the plastic impeller vanes or deep in the sump.
2. Check the grey drain hose at the back of the machine to ensure it isn't kinked or crushed against the wall. Once you've done this, let me know what you find.

I've checked the drain hose behind the machine and it looks fine, not kinked or squashed, and it goes into the standpipe under the sink. I haven't looked into the filter opening with a torch yet, but I can do that. Anything else I should do once I've done that?

E18 means the machine detected that water did not drain within the expected time. Does it spin completely freely, or do you feel any resistance? Also check if there is any debris stuck behind the vanes. If it feels notchy or blocked, that suggests why E18 appeared.

I've already turned the impeller by finger and it was slightly notchy at first and then free. I haven't looked in with a torch yet though. Once I've cleaned out the sock, hair grip and fluff, what should I do next?

Once you've removed all the debris and rinsed the filter housing, please do two things: first, shine a torch into the opening to check that no small items (like coins or beads) are stuck behind where the impeller sits. Second, put the filter back in tightly, plug the machine in, and run a 'Drain & Spin' programme. Does it drain successfully without showing E18 again?

I cleaned the filter, put it back in tightly and ran the drain and spin programme. It drained quickly, E18 has gone and it spins normally now. I'm not sure what to look for with the torch, so I didn't do that bit. Is there anything else I should do?

That is excellent news. You do not need to do anything else right now. To help prevent this from happening again, I recommend checking the filter every few months or if you notice the wash cycle taking longer than usual. Also, always check pockets before washing, especially for small items like hair grips or coins.
